note: Renovation work plan for A501. Edit in the app (Work plan page) or here. Sizes are from the model, not site measurements.

tasks.title: Measure the rooms on site and compare with the plan
tasks.detail: The model uses floor-plan sizes. Measure the Drawing Room north wall, the entry pocket, the entry door leaf and the window sill before ordering anything.

tasks.title: Get the builder or structural engineer to approve every wall opening
tasks.detail: Three openings need approval: the cabinet door through the 9-inch Drawing Room north wall, the entry pocket, and the wall to be removed on the left after the entry for the shoe rack. Ask which walls are load-bearing and what support (lintel or beam) each needs.
tasks.needs: Structural approval before any cutting

tasks.title: Inspect the shaft behind the Drawing Room north wall before any work
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: it is an open shaft with no floor (first floor); permission to close it has been received. Before cutting: confirm from the entry side how wide and deep the opening is, where the concrete slab edges are at the south and north ends and how thick they are, and whether any pipes, cables or ducts run in the shaft and need access later. The east part of the pocket holds an existing cabinet, so find out what it stands on.

tasks.title: Get housing-society permission for civil work and the new main gate
tasks.detail: Many societies need notice or permission for wall changes, debris removal hours and a change to the outer door or gate.
tasks.needs: Society permission

tasks.title: Finalise the entry ceiling: long PVC ceiling planks
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the entry ceiling will be PVC. Square 24 x 24 inch tiles were considered and dropped the same day: the entry is only about 1.0 m wide, so a 610 mm tile fits barely one and a half times across. Instead use LONG PVC ceiling planks (the interlocking strip type, commonly about 250 mm wide and sold in 3 m lengths), finalised after visiting some shops. Proposed: run them along the length of the entry (about 2.1 m), so each plank is one piece with no end joints and about four planks cover the width. Lights: recessed round LED panel lights, the type already used in the home (Orient Electric 12 W recessed panel, 1,200 lumens), but single-colour, not the 3-in-1 colour-changing version. Proposed, not yet agreed by the owner: neutral white (4000 K), two lights of 6-8 W each along the length, on one switch at the door. Still to decide: the plank width, design and colour, the edge trim, the height the ceiling drops to, and whether anything above must stay reachable. Nothing is drawn in the 3D model yet.
tasks.needs: Owner to visit shops and choose the plank; confirm plank direction, light colour (neutral white proposed) and count (two proposed)

tasks.title: Electrician to survey existing wiring, earthing and the distribution board
tasks.detail: Confirm existing points, MCB/RCBO ratings, the AC rating, and where intercom, broadband and DTH cables enter.

tasks.title: List the plumbing changes wanted
tasks.detail: No plumbing change is recorded in the project yet. Decide: kitchen sink and water purifier points, washing machine, washroom fittings, balcony water heater. Add each as its own task.
tasks.needs: Owner decision

tasks.title: Freeze the furniture layouts that fix where points and openings go
tasks.detail: Electrical points follow the furniture (Drawing Room layout C). Confirm layouts before chasing walls.

tasks.title: Drawing Room AC: choose the size, the indoor position and where the outdoor unit goes
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the Drawing Room has no AC; one has to be bought. The room is about 3.35 x 5.34 m (18 sq m, 193 sq ft), but its east side is open to the Lobby/Dining (about 16 sq m more), so the AC cools both unless that opening can be closed. Starting point: an inverter split AC of 1.5 ton if only the Drawing Room is cooled, 2 ton if the opening stays open; ask the dealer to confirm for the top-floor heat and sun on the south window. The electrical plan already has the AC point on the west wall, 3,080 mm from the north wall and 2,300 high, above the west sofa. Decide where the outdoor unit hangs, because that fixes the pipe route and its length. Update 2026-10-04: glass sliding doors between the Drawing Room and the Lobby are decided, so the AC can be sized for the Drawing Room alone (about 1.5 ton), to be confirmed by the dealer.
tasks.needs: Owner decision: tonnage and model; indoor wall; outdoor unit position (society rules may apply)

tasks.title: Drawing Room: finalise layered lighting with track lights (no false ceiling)
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04, decided: track lights plus the existing chandelier, no false ceiling, no table lamps and no swing-arm wall lights. The room has TWO ceiling fans (one at each end) and the chandelier midway between them. Drawn in the 3D model (Drawing Room, layout C): 48 V magnetic surface track, white, fixed straight to the slab. Track 1, 2.0 m, parallel to the TV wall and 400 mm in front of it: three 7 W spot heads (about 600 lumens each, 24-36 degree beam, anti-glare) aimed at the fluted panel, none at the screen. Track 2, 2.7 m, along the west wall 600 mm off it, over the sofas: two 15 W diffused linear heads (about 1,400 lumens each) between the two fans, and three 12 W READING heads (about 1,000 lumens each, 36 degree beam) pointing straight down at the seats: the two ends of the west sofa and the west end of the south sofa. Reading is done by turning these up; they are dimmed or off otherwise. Totals: 4.7 m of track, 8 heads, 87 W, about 7,600 lumens, all dimmable. One 48 V 150 W driver, hidden where it can be reached (the cap of the panel wall). IMPORTANT for the dimming to work as intended: Track 2 needs its own dimmer, separate from Track 1, and ideally the reading heads are separately controllable from the diffused heads (smart heads, or a two-circuit track); a plain single-circuit track dims every head on it together. Colour: warm white 3000 K for the spots; the diffused and reading heads may be the tunable 3-in-1 type, neutral white being better for long reading. Mood light: dim the tracks, and use colour-changing (RGB + warm white) LED strip for the strip on top of the TV panel and the glow under the south sofa. Keep downward heads out from under the fan blades. The fan and chandelier positions in the model are assumed.
tasks.needs: MEASURE: where the two fans and the chandelier are (distance from the walls) and the fan blade diameter. DECIDE at the shop: how the reading heads are dimmed separately (smart heads or a two-circuit track). Buy track, heads and driver from one maker so they fit each other

tasks.title: Lobby / Dining: finalise track lighting (no false ceiling)
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: track lights in the Lobby too, for flexibility. Drawn in the 3D model: the same 48 V magnetic surface track as the Drawing Room, white, fixed to the slab, in two runs that hug the walls so the middle of the ceiling stays free. Track 1, 2.6 m, along the south wall about 500 mm off it, east of the toilet door: two 7 W spots on the wall and two 15 W diffused heads for general light. Track 2, 1.5 m, in front of the ironing storage on the east wall: one 7 W spot on the storage doors and one 12 W down spot over the pulled-out ironing board. The linear pendant over the dining table stays. Totals: 4.1 m of track, 6 heads, 63 W, about 5,600 lumens, one 48 V 100 W driver, all dimmable, warm white 3000 K. Use the same maker as the Drawing Room so heads can be swapped between rooms.
tasks.needs: Is there a ceiling fan in the Lobby, and where? Confirm the two track positions; where the driver hides

tasks.title: Remove the window on the left after the main door and the wall below it, for the shoe rack
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: on the left after entering the main door there is a window with about 4 ft (about 1,220 mm) of wall below it. The window and that wall both come out, so the opening runs from the floor, and the shoe rack replaces them. Keep or add a lintel over the opening, make the cut edges straight and plastered, and close off anything left open to the outside. The opening width is not measured yet.
tasks.needs: Structural approval; measure the opening width and the window height

tasks.title: Fix an iron-angle support frame for the shoe rack to stand on
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: before the shoe rack goes in, something has to carry it, ideally an iron angle. A welded angle frame (a base the size of the rack, with brackets or legs) anchored into the wall and the slab edge, set level. Because it sits in an opening to the outside, use galvanised or stainless angle, or mild steel with anti-rust primer and two coats of paint. The fabricator sizes the angle for a full rack of shoes plus the cabinet itself; ask the engineer to confirm the fixing into the wall.
tasks.needs: Final shoe rack size, so the frame matches it: 15 in (381 mm) deep is decided; height about 6 1/2 ft and the width are to be confirmed

tasks.title: Cut the cabinet door opening in the Drawing Room north wall
tasks.detail: Opening 500 wide x 1800 high at the west end of the north wall (100-600 mm from the west wall), with a lintel, into the west half of the entry pocket. Kept only as wide as a person needs (490 clear) so it can be hidden in the wall panelling. Behind this wall is an open shaft with no floor: fix a barrier across the opening as soon as it is cut and keep it until the steel floor is in.
tasks.needs: Structural approval

tasks.title: West cabinet: steel floor over the open shaft
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the space behind the Drawing Room north wall is an open shaft on the first floor with NO floor, and permission to close it has been received. After the mason cuts the wall, a steel floor is built across the shaft and the storage stands on it. Proposal (pictures: docs/drawings/west-cabinet-platform-steps.png, and the measured drawing docs/drawings/west-cabinet-platform.png): A, a 50 x 50 x 6 angle bolted along the west wall with M10 anchors every 300 mm, its ends also resting 150 mm on the concrete; B, on the east side where there is no wall, a 50 x 50 x 3 square hollow section spanning north to south, resting 150 mm on the concrete floor at each end on a base plate, anchors at least 100 mm in from the slab edge; C, angles across the two ends; D, cross members between A and B no more than 300 mm apart; then a 5 mm chequered steel plate welded on, and 19 mm waterproof plywood over it. Anti-rust primer and paint. About 650 wide x 1,100 front to back, from the model, not measured. Alternative to price: a cast concrete slab doweled into the slab edges, which also seals smell, noise and pests from the shaft.
tasks.needs: SAFETY: this is a floor over a drop. A structural engineer must design and sign it off (as a floor, typically 200-300 kg per square metre, not for one 100 kg person). Keep the society permission in writing. Check for pipes or cables in the shaft that still need access. Barrier the opening and stop anything falling down the shaft while work is open.

tasks.title: Build the partition that splits the entry pocket into two cabinets
tasks.detail: Full-height partition about 736 mm from the Drawing Room west wall line; the east cabinet stays open to the entry gallery.

tasks.title: Replace the iron main entry door (the first, outer door) with a stainless steel one
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-03, confirmed 2026-10-04: the existing first door at the entry is iron; replace it with stainless steel. Measure the opening, choose grade 304 (or 316 near the coast), design, lock and finish; remove the old door and fix the new frame.
tasks.needs: Choose design, lock and finish; get a fabricator quote

tasks.title: Replace the plain iron shaft cover at the entry with a better-looking one
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: on the right-hand side at the entry a plain iron cover closes the services shaft. Replace it with something more pleasing. It must still open or lift off for access to the shaft, and stay ventilated if the present one is. Options to price: a stainless steel louvred door matching the new entry door; a powder-coated aluminium louvre panel; or a flush panel door finished like the entry joinery. Size not yet measured.
tasks.needs: Choose the type; measure the opening; check with the society, since the shaft is shared

tasks.title: Remove debris and make good the cut edges
tasks.detail: Plaster the reveals of every new opening ready for frames.

tasks.title: Plumbing first fix: pipes and drains in walls and floor
tasks.detail: Do this before plaster and tiles. Pressure-test before closing the walls.

tasks.title: Chase walls and fix conduits and boxes for the 17 Drawing Room points
tasks.detail: TV box behind the screen, media and router points behind the TV console with a 50 mm HDMI conduit between them, main switchboard on the east wall, AC point, sofa charging points, lights and the closet light.

tasks.title: TV wall: power and cable points behind the TV and the console
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (electrician): power for the TV, the router and the music system, with no cables showing. Do this before the panelling goes on. (1) Behind the TV, inside its outline but clear of the bracket: a recessed box with 2 sockets for the TV and one spare. (2) Behind the console, about 400 mm high: a box with 2 sockets (one feeds the power strip inside the console, one spare), and beside it the data box for broadband, LAN, phone and intercom. (3) A 50 mm flexible conduit from the TV box down to the console box, with a pull wire, for HDMI, optical and LAN cables, so they can be changed later without opening the wall. (4) Feed these sockets by their own cable from the distribution board on a 16 A breaker with earth-leakage protection, not looped off the old switchboard. Conduits can be clipped to the wall surface because the panelling stands 20-25 mm off the wall on battens; chase only where there is no panel.
tasks.needs: Final TV size and bracket position, so the box is hidden for both the 55 and the 65 inch TV

tasks.title: Replace the old Drawing Room switchboard with a modular switch plate
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (electrician): the existing switchboard is on the north wall on the east side of the TV, about 10 cm from the wall end, at about the middle height of the TV, and it falls inside the area the panelling will cover. It controls this room's fans and lights and has a power socket. Replace it in the same place with a modular plate: take out the old board, fit a modular metal box of the right size (count the modules: one per light switch, two per fan regulator, two per socket, plus one or two spare), re-terminate the existing wires and check each for damaged insulation and a proper earth. Use step or electronic fan regulators of the same modular range. Set the new box forward by the panel build-up (18 mm panel plus the 20-25 mm batten gap) with a box extension ring, so the plate ends up flush on the panel face. The plate itself is fitted after painting. Decided 2026-10-04: no switchboard on the east wall; this board stays the room's only one, so point E1 of the earlier electrical plan is dropped (the 3D model still shows it until the board is measured).
tasks.needs: MEASURE: the board's width and height, its distance from the entry door frame, and the height of its centre. CHECK: that the TV does not cover it (a 55-inch TV centred as drawn ends 120 mm from the door frame; a 65-inch ends 10 mm from it). Count the fans, lights and sockets; choose the modular range and colour

tasks.title: Decide and install the optional floor box at the coffee table
tasks.detail: Must be chased into the floor before any flooring work.
tasks.needs: Owner decision

tasks.title: Run CAT6, coax, phone and intercom cables to the TV wall
tasks.detail: Low-voltage cables in their own conduits; cross mains only at right angles.

tasks.title: Plan electrical points for the other rooms
tasks.detail: Only the Drawing Room and the Balcony office have a point plan so far.
tasks.needs: Plan not made yet

tasks.title: Entry ceiling: run the wiring for the lights and their switch
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (electrician). Before the PVC ceiling goes up: chase a conduit from a switch box beside the main door up the wall, and run it on the slab above the ceiling line to each light position, leaving about 300 mm of spare wire at each point. Two light points are proposed, on one switch. Take the supply from the nearest lighting circuit. Mark the light positions on the slab from the plank layout so they land where the cut-outs will be.
tasks.needs: Light count and positions, and the switch position, from the entry ceiling plan

tasks.title: Drawing Room AC: lay the copper pipes, drain pipe and cable before plaster
tasks.detail: AC installer, before plastering and painting. Core a 65-75 mm hole through the outer wall, sloping slightly down to the outside. Run the insulated copper pipe pair, the drain pipe and the link cable from the indoor position to the outdoor unit, either chased into the wall or in a neat PVC casing. The drain must fall all the way (at least 1 in 100) and end at a proper drain point, not drip on a neighbour. Keep the pipe run as short as possible (ideally under 5 m) with few bends. Leave the pipe ends sealed and labelled.
tasks.needs: The AC model, so the pipe sizes match; the outdoor unit position

tasks.title: Drawing Room AC: dedicated power line and socket
tasks.detail: Electrician. A separate circuit for the AC from the distribution board: its own 20 A breaker, 4 sq mm copper wire with earth, to a 20/25 A AC socket or a switch with indicator beside the indoor unit (planned on the west wall, 2,300 high). Nothing else on this circuit. Add a voltage stabiliser point only if the chosen AC needs one.

tasks.title: Drawing Room: power feed points for the track lights and wall lights
tasks.detail: Electrician. One feed point at the wall end of each track, brought up inside the wall and across the wall-ceiling corner, so no wire shows on the slab; the track itself carries the power along its length. A separate switched and dimmed line for each track back to the switchboard, and for each layer if a two-circuit track is used. Fix the 48 V 150 W driver where it can be reached, for example inside the cap of the panel wall; check the dimmer type matches the driver. Take down the old small wall light in the north-west and the wall reading light, and either reuse their wiring as the track feeds or close the points with blank plates.

tasks.title: Lobby / Dining: power feed points for the track lights
tasks.detail: Electrician. One feed point at the wall end of each of the two tracks, brought up inside the wall, each track on its own dimmed line; the dining pendant on a separate switch. Fix the 48 V 100 W driver where it can be reached.

tasks.title: Close chases, plaster and level the walls
Flooring and skirting repairs where walls were cut
Optional: replace the old projecting skirting with modern flush skirting
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the present skirting is the old type that sticks out from the wall, so dust collects on its top edge and in the corners. Replace it along the walls with a modern skirting that sits in line with the wall. Options to price: (1) flush skirting, a tile or stone strip set into the plaster so its face is level with the wall, with a thin groove above it; (2) a recessed aluminium profile that leaves a shadow gap; (3) a slim 50-60 mm tile skirting with a straight top edge, the cheapest and least dusty of the surface types. Options 1 and 2 need the wall base chased and re-plastered, so they are done with the plaster work and before painting. Running length not yet measured.
tasks.needs: OPTIONAL (owner 2026-10-04: a lot of work for the whole home). Decide before plaster work starts: do it, do only some rooms, or skip
tasks.notes: If done, it must be finished before painting. Skipping it does not hold up anything else.

tasks.title: Fit the entry ceiling: long PVC planks on a frame
tasks.detail: Fix a level frame of battens or metal channels to the slab, then clip the PVC planks on and finish the edges with trim. The light wiring must already be in place above (electrician). The entry is about 2.1 m long by 1.0 m clear wide on the plan. Set the planks out from the centre line so the two edge planks are cut to the same width, and add a batten above each light position to carry the light. The electrician cuts the light openings and fits the lights afterwards.
tasks.needs: Plank chosen

tasks.title: West cabinet: build the box on the steel floor, shelves and the hidden door
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (carpenter). On the steel floor over the shaft: lay the 19 mm waterproof (BWP) plywood floor board, then build the cabinet box (two sides, back and top, in 18 mm waterproof plywood, laminated inside) so nothing is open to the shaft, and fit shelves 380 deep at the back. Door: one flush 500 x 1800 leaf on concealed hinges, hinged on its west edge, no handle (push latch), opening OUT into the Drawing Room, faced with the same fluted slats as the wall panelling so it cannot be seen. For winter clothes, opened about twice a year. Leave a small vent at the top and bottom of the box so clothes do not get musty.

tasks.title: Clean panel wall behind the TV that hides the cabinet door
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (carpenter). Fluted panelling on the north wall from 40 to 2100 mm from the west wall, floor to 1800 high, 18 thick, a groove every 100 mm set out from the hidden door so both door edges fall on a groove; a slim cap with a light strip on top. Fix it on 20-25 mm battens, not straight on the wall: the gap behind is where the electrician runs the TV and console cables, so the wall need not be chased. SWITCHBOARD: the existing board (east of the TV, mid-TV height) falls inside the panel. Do not flute that part: make the east end of the panelling a plain flat strip, about 250 mm wide and full height, in the same finish, and cut one clean rectangular opening in it for the modular box; the switch plate then sits flat and covers the cut edge. A plate cannot sit flat across grooves. Also cut neat openings for the socket boxes behind the TV and behind the console. Fix a plywood backing piece behind the panel where the TV bracket bolts through into the wall.
tasks.needs: Panel finish and colour; exact switchboard size and position (the electrician fits the box first, then the carpenter cuts to it)

tasks.title: TV console under the TV (one piece, drag-out)
tasks.detail: Console 1600 x 400 x 400 on 200 legs with glides, 500-2100 from the west wall, free-standing so it can be dragged 600 out when the hidden door is used: router bay and Bass Module bay with open lattice, storage with a lattice door. Inside, screw a 6-way surge-protected power strip to the back panel; the router, set-top box, soundbar and Bass Module plug into it, so only ONE mains lead, one LAN cable and one HDMI or optical cable leave the console, each with about 1 m of slack. Cut a 60 mm cable hole with a brush grommet in the back panel and in each bay divider, and leave vent slots behind the router and Bass Module.

tasks.title: New shoe rack on the left after the main door, on the iron-angle support
tasks.detail: Built to sit on the support frame in the opening where the window and the wall below it were. Depth: 15 in (381 mm) overall, decided by the owner 2026-10-04, so shoes go in lengthwise, toe to the back; that leaves about 340 mm clear inside after an 18 mm door and the back panel. Height about 6 1/2 ft (about 1,980 mm): the owner will confirm, so treat it as provisional. Width to suit the opening. The back and sides that face outside need a weatherproof finish (exterior-grade board or a metal or tile cladding) and a sealed joint to the wall. The 3D model draws the rack 865 wide x 2,134 (7 ft) high x 381 deep; width and height are updated once confirmed.
tasks.needs: TO BE CONFIRMED: height (about 6 1/2 ft) and width; measure the opening and the wall thickness

tasks.title: Fold-down seat at the entry for changing shoes
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-09-29, added to the plan 2026-10-04: a wall-hinged seat a person can sit on to change shoes, which folds flat against the wall when not in use. As drawn in the 3D model: on the west wall beside the shoe rack, seat 360 wide x 340 deep, 460 mm above the floor, on two folding support brackets with a hinge along the wall edge; these are model sizes, not site measurements. Use heavy-duty folding brackets rated for at least 120 kg and fix them into solid masonry with anchor bolts, not into plaster alone. Folded, it should project no more than about 60 mm so the 1.0 m wide entry stays clear.
tasks.needs: Confirm the wall and position once the shoe rack is in; choose the seat finish

tasks.title: Other carpentry: wardrobes, kitchen cabinets, study, pooja, balcony office
tasks.detail: One line for now. Split into a task per room when each design is frozen.
tasks.needs: Split per room

tasks.title: Drawing Room south window: replace the fixed centre section with two outward-opening shutters, and glaze them
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (carpenter). The south window has a wooden frame in three sections; the two side sections have shutters opening outward and the centre section is fixed. Take out the fixed centre panel and make two wooden shutters for it that open outward, so all three sections match: two shutters each, six in all. Copy the existing shutters exactly (wood, section sizes, mouldings, rail heights) so the new pair cannot be told apart. Hardware to match the old: hinges, a tower bolt top and bottom, a handle, and a stay or hook to hold each shutter open in wind. Glass: 5 mm clear glass, toughened if the pane is large or low, bedded in sealant and fixed with wooden beading; check the old panes at the same time and replace any that are cracked or loose. The owner confirms (2026-10-04) that nothing outside blocks the centre shutters; keep it that way when the AC outdoor unit is placed. The window is about 2.3 m wide and from 550 to 2,100 mm above the floor in the model; the three section widths are not measured. Note (owner 2026-10-04): the top of the window, about 1 ft, is a fixed band across the sections; the new centre shutters are made for the opening part below it, the same height as the existing side shutters.
tasks.needs: Measure the three sections; glass type (clear, frosted or tinted)

tasks.title: Putty, primer and paint
tasks.detail: After carpentry carcasses are in, before fixtures.

tasks.title: Drawing Room south window: change the white paint to a wooden shade
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the window on the south wall is painted white; give it a wooden shade. The frame is wood (confirmed). Strip the white paint from the frame and all six shutters, sand to bare wood, stain to the chosen shade and finish with PU or melamine polish, two or three coats; on the outside faces use an exterior-grade finish, because they get sun and rain. The two new centre shutters are finished together with the old ones so the colour is the same. Match the shade to the TV panel wall and console so the room has one wood tone. Do this before the walls get their final coat, and mask the glass.
tasks.needs: The wood shade

tasks.title: Fit switches, sockets, USB chargers and light fittings; test every circuit
tasks.detail: Includes the RCBO test, earth test and labelling the board. Also fix the track lights to the slab, clip in and aim the heads after the furniture is in place.

tasks.title: Fit taps, sanitary ware and appliances; leak test
Mount the TV and connect the soundbar, Bass Module, router, landline and intercom
tasks.detail: Bolt the TV bracket through the panel and its backing into the wall. Plug the TV into the box behind it. Run HDMI, optical and LAN through the conduit down to the console. Everything in the console plugs into the power strip inside it, which plugs into the wall socket behind. Tie the three leads that leave the console into one loom with 1 m of slack, so the console can be dragged out.

tasks.title: Entry ceiling: fit the lights and the switch, and test
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04 (electrician). Cut the round openings in the PVC planks, connect and clip in the recessed LED panel lights (single colour; neutral white proposed), fit the switch plate at the door and test. Each driver sits above the ceiling on the batten, not resting on the PVC.

tasks.title: Drawing Room AC: fit the indoor and outdoor units and commission
tasks.detail: After painting. Fix the indoor unit level on its plate and the outdoor unit on a rust-proof stand, connect the pipes, vacuum the lines, release the gas, check the drain by pouring water, and run a cooling test. Keep the warranty card and the installer's details in the task notes.

tasks.title: Drawing Room south window: fit a roller mosquito net on each of the three sections
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04, decided: a roller mesh for each of the three sections, on the room side, because all six shutters open outward and a hand must reach their handles and bolts. Each roller has its cassette at the top or at one side of the section, side guide channels so the mesh cannot blow out or leave a gap, and a bottom bar that latches. Fibreglass mesh; cassette and channels coloured to match the new wooden shade. Fix them to the wooden frame after it is polished. The south sofa stands under this window, so place the pull or latch where it can be reached over the sofa back. The top fixed band (about 1 ft) needs no net: each roller covers only the opening part below it, with its cassette under the transom.
tasks.needs: Measure the clear opening of each section after the centre shutters are made; cassette at the top (pull down) or at the side (pull across)

tasks.title: Sliding doors between the Drawing Room and the Lobby: aluminium frame, fluted glass, nothing on the floor
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04, decided: slim aluminium frame with fluted glass, and NOTHING on the floor. The opening is about 3,280 mm wide and about 2,395 mm high under the hanging beam (model sizes, not measured). How to build it: top-hung sliding panels, all the weight carried by a track fixed under the beam, no floor track. Three panels of about 1,100 mm on a three-line (telescopic) track, linked panel to panel at the bottom so they steady each other; the only guide is one small fitting at the parking end, beside the wall and out of the walking line. Proposed: extend the track about 1.1 m past the opening along the solid wall north of it, so the panels park in front of that wall and the whole opening is clear. Glass: 8 mm toughened, fluted (vertical flutes); if toughened fluted glass is hard to find locally, use clear toughened glass with a fluted film. Soft-close dampers; brush seals at the top and between panels and a brush strip along each bottom edge, to hold the AC cooling; recessed flush pulls. Each panel weighs roughly 55-60 kg, about 180 kg in all, hanging from the beam. PVC folding and crystal folding were considered and dropped. The 3D model still draws a 10-panel folding partition.
tasks.needs: Measure the opening width and the height under the beam; engineer or fabricator to confirm the beam takes about 180 kg on anchors; which side the panels park on (Drawing Room or Lobby face of the wall); frame colour

tasks.title: Drawing Room south window: roll-up sun screen (bamboo chick) on the outside
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the window faces south-west and takes a lot of sun and heat in the Delhi summer; a curtain is used now. A roll-up screen (bamboo chick) on the outside stops the heat before it comes through the glass. New information from the owner: the top of the window, about 1 ft, is a FIXED band, and the opening shutters start below it; there is a cover above the window. Design (drawing: docs/drawings/south-window-chick-cord.png): hang the screen close to the wall, about 85 mm out, from hooks just under the frame head. Rolled UP, the roll (about 100 mm across) parks in front of the fixed band, above the shutters, so all six shutters open freely under it. Rolled DOWN, it covers the whole window; the shutters must be shut first, which they are on a hot afternoon with the AC on. The pull cord comes INTO the room through a small lined hole (brass or ceramic eyelet) in the frame head and ties on a hook inside, so it is worked from inside. Hook the bottom rail to two hooks at the sill when it is down, so wind cannot swing it. Width about 2.5 m, drop about 1.7 m. Stainless steel hooks. Plain bamboo lasts two or three monsoons outside; a PVC-coated or HDPE outdoor screen looks similar and lasts longer. This replaces the earlier idea of hanging it 450 mm out from the edge of the cover: no long brackets, less wind sway, better shade.
